screening_decisions.reason: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary randomized controlled trial (RCT).
This is a symposium summary/educational review article, not an RCT.

This is an RCT comparing two different timing regimens of cabergoline (a dopamine agonist) for preventing OHSS in women undergoing IVF. It meets the population, intervention, and study design criteria.
This is an RCT comparing cabergoline alone, coasting alone, and their combination for preventing OHSS in high-risk IVF/ICSI patients. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a case report describing a single patient, not an RCT.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating cabergoline for preventing moderate OHSS in high-risk IVF patients. Meets all criteria.
This is a nested case-control study focusing on cardiac valve regurgitation in patients with Parkinson's disease or restless legs syndrome. It does not involve ART or OHSS prevention.
This is a preclinical animal study (rats) investigating a VEGF receptor-2 inhibitor, not a dopamine agonist RCT in humans.
This is a Cochrane systematic review comparing GnRH antagonists with agonists. It does not evaluate dopamine agonists.
This is a cross-sectional study assessing cardiac valve abnormalities in patients treated for hyperprolactinemia. It is unrelated to ART or OHSS prevention.
This is a retrospective case-control study comparing IVM with standard IVF. It does not evaluate dopamine agonists and is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT.
This is a case report involving spontaneous OHSS due to pituitary adenomas, not ART-induced OHSS, and is not an RCT.
This is a clinical trial for cancer treatment using SU5416. It is completely unrelated to ART or OHSS.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating quinagolide (a dopamine agonist) for preventing early OHSS in IVF patients. Meets all criteria.
This is a prospective RCT comparing cabergoline with no medication for preventing early OHSS in high-risk ART patients. Meets all criteria.
This is a narrative review article summarizing existing evidence, not a primary RCT.
This is an editorial/review discussing various IVF techniques. It does not evaluate dopamine agonists and is not an RCT.
This is primarily a preclinical animal study (rats) investigating the mechanism of cabergoline. Although it briefly mentions clinical application, it does not report a human RCT.
This is a case report on spontaneous OHSS caused by an LH-secreting pituitary adenoma. It is not ART-induced and is not an RCT.

This study compares IVF versus ICSI fertilization techniques in in-vitro maturation (IVM) cycles for PCOS patients. It does not involve dopamine agonists or OHSS prevention as the intervention. The research question is about fertilization methods, not OHSS prophylaxis.

This is an RCT comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) 0.5mg for 8 days versus no treatment for OHSS prevention in 70 women at high risk undergoing IVF/ICSI. Primary outcome was incidence of OHSS. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention focus, ART population.

Despite the title mentioning cabergoline and OHSS, the abstract content is entirely about bacterial vaginosis (BV) and abnormal vaginal microbiota in IVF patients. The abstract describes a meta-analysis of BV risks in IVF, with outcomes including live birth rate and spontaneous abortion. This appears to be a mismatched abstract or unrelated study content. Does not meet criteria for dopamine agonist OHSS prevention RCT.

This is a Cochrane review evaluating volume expanders (albumin, HES, mannitol, etc.) for OHSS prevention. It is not an RCT, and the intervention is not a dopamine agonist. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) versus intravenous human albumin for OHSS prevention in 138 high-risk women. Outcomes included moderate and severe OHSS incidence. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist compared with another intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, not an individual RCT itself. While it synthesizes evidence on cabergoline for OHSS prevention, it does not meet the selection criteria for primary RCT studies.

This is a clinical guidance/review article that reevaluates OHSS prevention techniques. It is not an RCT. While it mentions dopamine receptor agonists as potential treatments, it is a literature review providing clinical guidance, not a primary research study.

This is an RCT comparing GnRH antagonist rescue protocol combined with cabergoline versus cabergoline alone for OHSS prevention in 236 high-risk patients. Outcomes included moderate/severe OHSS incidence, pregnancy rates, and oocyte retrieval parameters. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.

This is a review article discussing dopamine agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine) for treating hyperprolactinaemia and their association with cardiac valvular disease. It does not address OHSS prevention in ART, nor is it an RCT.

This is a very brief abstract/commentary discussing the role of VEGF in OHSS pathophysiology and how dopamine agonists may prevent/treat OHSS by blocking VEGF receptor expression. It is not an RCT and does not present primary research data.

This is a review article discussing VEGF/VEGFR-2 pathophysiology in OHSS. While it mentions a trial of 69 oocyte donors with cabergoline vs placebo, the article itself is a literature review, not the primary RCT report. Does not meet RCT selection criteria.

This is a commentary/review discussing GnRH agonist triggering for OHSS prevention and its potential mechanism involving PEDF. It mentions dopamine agonists in passing but is not an RCT evaluating dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention.

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind RCT comparing cabergoline 0.5mg/day versus placebo in 69 oocyte donors at risk of OHSS. Outcomes included hemoconcentration, ascites, and moderate OHSS incidence (20% vs 43.8%, P=0.04). Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist vs placebo, OHSS prevention in ART.

This is a nested case-control study examining cardiac valve regurgitation risk with dopamine agonists in Parkinson's disease and hyperprolactinaemia patients. It does not involve ART, OHSS prevention, or RCT design. Completely different population and research question.

The abstract explicitly states this is a 'non randomized clinical trial' comparing cabergoline-treated group (50 women) with historical controls (25 women). Since it is not an RCT, it does not meet the selection criteria.

This is a case series of 4 patients describing an outpatient treatment protocol for OHSS (treatment, not prevention). It is not an RCT and focuses on treating established OHSS rather than preventing it.

This is a symposium abstract providing an overview of OHSS pathophysiology and dopamine agonist mechanisms. It is not an RCT and does not present primary research data on dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention.

This is an RCT comparing IV calcium gluconate versus cabergoline (dopamine agonist) for OHSS prevention in 202 high-risk patients undergoing IVF. Outcomes included OHSS occurrence and severity. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist compared with another intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.

This appears to be a Cochrane review protocol/abstract (presented in Spanish) describing the objectives to evaluate cabergoline for OHSS prevention. It is not an individual RCT but rather a review protocol.

This is explicitly described as a 'prospective cohort study' (not an RCT) comparing cabergoline vs no medication in 41 women with PCOS. Outcomes were follicular fluid hormone levels (IGF-I, AMH, inhibin B, HGF), not OHSS incidence or live birth rate. Does not meet RCT selection criteria.

This study is about VEGF blocking therapy for cancer treatment, not about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention in ART. Wrong population (cancer patients), wrong intervention (anti-angiogenic agents), and wrong context.
This is a review article summarizing OHSS classifications and preventive measures. It is not an RCT and does not test dopamine agonists specifically.

This is a cross-sectional study about valvular heart disease in prolactinoma patients treated with dopamine agonists. Wrong population (prolactinoma, not ART), wrong outcome (cardiac effects, not OHSS prevention), and not an RCT.
This is a review article about cabergoline for OHSS, not an RCT. Reviews do not meet the study design criteria.
This is a brief update/review about PCOS infertility treatment. It does not focus on dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention and is not an RCT.
This is a review article about ART complications including OHSS. It is not an RCT and does not test dopamine agonists.

This is an RCT (95 high-risk infertile women randomly divided into two groups) comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) versus albumin for OHSS prevention in ART. Meets all selection criteria: correct population (ART patients at high risk for OHSS), correct intervention (cabergoline), correct comparator (another intervention), and relevant outcomes (OHSS incidence, pregnancy rates).
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it analyzes RCTs of dopamine agonists, the study itself is a secondary publication.

This is a prospective controlled study (n=250) comparing laparoscopic ovarian drilling versus GnRH antagonist combined with cabergoline for OHSS prevention in women with CCR-PCOD who had severe OHSS previously. While the design is described as 'prospective controlled' rather than explicitly randomized, it involves cabergoline as part of the intervention for OHSS prevention in ART. Given the conservative approach (include when uncertain), this should be included for further review.
This is a Cochrane review about coasting for OHSS prevention, not an RCT. While it mentions some comparisons with cabergoline, the study itself is a systematic review.
This is a Cochrane review about metformin for PCOS women undergoing IVF/ICSI. It does not focus on dopamine agonists and is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review about coasting for OHSS prevention, not an RCT. Does not test dopamine agonists.
This is a Cochrane review about luteal phase support methods in ART. It does not focus on dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention and is not an RCT.
This is an animal study (rats and mice) about VEGF inhibition and uterine edema. Wrong species, wrong intervention (VEGF antiserum, not dopamine agonists), and not an RCT in humans.

This is an RCT (28 women randomly divided into two groups) comparing bromocriptine (dopamine agonist) versus folic acid (placebo-like control) for OHSS prevention in IVF patients. Meets selection criteria: correct population (IVF patients at high risk), correct intervention (bromocriptine), correct comparator (placebo/no active intervention), and relevant outcomes (OHSS incidence, VEGF levels, kidney function).

This is explicitly described as a retrospective study with matched controls, not an RCT. The abstract states 'A retrospective study with endpoints of implantation and ongoing/term pregnancy rates.' Retrospective studies do not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a prospective randomized study comparing HES alone versus HES plus cabergoline for OHSS prevention in GnRH agonist IVF cycles. Meets selection criteria: correct population (IVF patients at risk for OHSS), correct intervention (cabergoline added to standard care), correct comparator (standard care without cabergoline), and relevant outcomes (OHSS incidence/severity, pregnancy rates).

This is a prospective study comparing bromocriptine-treated patients with a historical control group (matched for age and BMI). Historical controls do not constitute randomization, so this is not an RCT. The study design does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a review article examining evidence for various OHSS prevention strategies. It is not an RCT and does not primarily test dopamine agonists.
This is explicitly described as a retrospective study investigating bromocriptine treatment outcomes. Retrospective studies do not meet the RCT requirement in the selection criteria.

This is a clinical trial comparing cabergoline (a dopamine agonist) versus coasting (another intervention) for OHSS prevention in women at high risk undergoing ART. The study design appears to be an RCT comparing dopamine agonist with another intervention, which meets the selection criteria.

This is an animal study (rodent/mice) investigating the VEGF/VEGFR-2 pathway in corpora lutea. It does not involve dopamine agonists, does not address OHSS prevention, and is not conducted in humans undergoing ART. Does not meet any of the selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled study evaluating cabergoline (dopamine agonist) at 0.25mg versus no treatment for OHSS prevention in women at high risk undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment. The primary outcome was OHSS incidence. This meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART population.

This is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) versus no medication for OHSS prevention in high-risk women undergoing ART. The study reports on OHSS incidence and ART outcomes. This meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART population.

This study investigates valvular heart disease in patients taking dopamine agonists for Parkinson's disease. The population is Parkinson's disease patients, not women undergoing ART. The study does not address OHSS prevention. Does not meet the population or outcome criteria.
This is a review article about OHSS, not a randomized controlled trial. The selection criteria specifically require RCTs. Review articles do not meet the study design criteria for inclusion.
